name: New-crop dates
tile_uses: Yogurt, the salad, a plate with cheese
why_now: Nearly every Medjool in the country is grown in the desert two hours from here, in the Coachella and Bard valleys, and they're picked from late summer through October. The ones on shelves now are this year's — soft, glossy, and much better than the ones that have been sitting since last fall.
how_to_choose: Plump and glossy, with skin that clings to the fruit
Soft enough to dent with a thumb
No crystallized sugar on the surface — that's age
A packed-on date printed on the box, if there is one
Yellow dates still on the branch are Barhi: crunchy and fresh, and only around for a few weeks
buy_this_much: 1 lb. They last for months in the fridge, so this is more about having them than using them up.
price_note: Costco and Middle Eastern markets are often half the supermarket price for the same Medjools.

flavor_paths.name: With salt
flavor_paths.description: Split, a few flakes of salt. Dessert.

flavor_paths.name: With cheese
flavor_paths.description: A sharp cheese or queso fresco. Sweet against salty.

flavor_paths.name: Torn into savory
flavor_paths.description: Into the arugula salad, or over roasted squash. Sweetness where you don't expect it.

weekday_uses: With a sharp cheese and a slice of Asian pear
weekend_use: Torn into the October salad, and a small plate of dates, guava, and queso fresco after the fish.
storage: In the fridge in a closed container for up to six months, or the counter for a few weeks. Cold dates firm up; let them sit out before eating.
one_thing_to_learn: A date is a fresh fruit that happens to dry well, not a dried fruit. Growers let them cure on the palm in the desert heat, which is why they're soft and sticky rather than leathery. Once you've eaten a new-crop Medjool, you'll notice the difference in the ones that aren't.
